newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Egenor to invest $99 mln up to 2000.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Egenor to invest $99 mln up to 2000.

text.p: Peruvian electricity generator Egenor said Friday it would spend $99 million up to 2000 in various investment projects.
"The total investment plan is $99 million for energy projects," Egenor's general manager William Gary Narron told a news conference.
He added that the investment, to be financed from company funds and a bank loan, would be concentrated on expansion projects at three generators in northern Peru.
Egenor operates two hydroelectric and seven thermal generators with an installed capacity of 408 megawatts (MW).
It is 60 percent owned by U.S. consortium Dominion Peru SA, which paid $228.2 million for its stake at the firm's 1996 privatization.
Dominion Resources Inc of the U.S. owns 97.6 percent of Dominion Peru, while U.S. citizens Marc T. Cox IV and Thomas F. Farrel each have a 1.2 percent stake in the group.

Narron said Egenor provisionally projects total investments of about $400 million in the next 10 years. These plans are "a show of confidence in the government and in the electricity sector," he added.
Jorge Palza, head of administration and finances for Egenor, said the generator hopes to start trading its shares on the Lima Stock Exchange in the first week of June.
He said the company posted $21 million profits in 1996, and up to April of this year had registered "a little more than $13 million" of profits.
